transcript.text: hoover washer drier showing EO3 wont drain, ive done the filter its clean. H3DS4965DACE. pump just buzzes. do i need a new pump??

To answer your question directly: not necessarily. A buzzing sound usually means the pump motor is trying to run but can't because something is physically stopping it—most commonly a coin, button, or piece of debris caught in the impeller blades. It could also be that the blockage is further down in the internal hoses. The next most useful check is to see if the pump itself is jammed. Please switch off and unplug the machine first for safety. 1. Remove the filter again (have a towel ready as some water may drip out).
2. Shine a torch into the hole where the filter was.
3. Gently try to turn the small plastic impeller you see inside with your finger. Tell me if it spins freely, or if it feels stuck/jammed by an object.
done that, power off. impeller spins totally freely, no resistance at all, feels like its not connected to anything. torch shows one fin looks snapped too

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump (jammed or failed)]
Yes, you need a new pump. The fact that the impeller spins freely and has a snapped fin suggests it is mechanically broken; the motor can no longer push water because the blades are damaged or detached. Please do not try to run the machine again as this will cause further damage or leaks. You will need to replace the drain pump assembly. As I cannot verify the exact part compatibility for your specific model number, please contact Hoover customer support or a qualified appliance engineer to source the correct replacement part and fit it safely.
